title: Why Light Before Bed Disrupts Your Sleep Cycle
hook: Your smartphone before bed is actively fighting your natural sleep.

narration.text: Your smartphone before bed is actively fighting your natural sleep.
Our bodies run on a 24-hour internal clock, called the circadian rhythm.
This rhythm largely responds to light and darkness cues from our environment.
Bright light, especially blue light, signals our brain that it is daytime.
This suppresses melatonin, the hormone that helps us feel sleepy.
Even a short exposure can delay the onset of natural sleepiness.
This makes it harder to fall asleep and reduces sleep quality.
Do you notice a difference in your sleep after using devices late?

description: Discover how light exposure, especially from screens, can significantly disrupt your body's natural sleep cycle. Understanding the science behind your circadian rhythm can help you improve your sleep quality.
topic: Why exposure to light before bed can disrupt your sleep cycle.
